one_liner: Pure-Zig network library with io_uring HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 engines; beats nginx, h2o and Drogon in HttpArena.
what_it_does: zix is a Zig 0.16 source module (no C, no libc linking, no third-party packages) that bundles server and client engines for raw TCP/UDP/UDS, HTTP/1.1 (zix.Http on std.http and the lean zix.Http1), HTTP/2 (h2c and h2), HTTP/3 over a pure-Zig QUIC, gRPC h2c, WebSocket, SSE, WebRTC data channels and FIX 4.x, plus pure-Zig TLS 1.3/1.2 on std.crypto and in-tree gzip/brotli. Handlers take a (Request, Response, Context) trio and are bound through a comptime Router; the dispatch model (.ASYNC, .EPOLL or .URING) is a required config field. It is a new framework, not a drop-in for nginx or any C/C++ server.
how_it_is_fast: Under .URING each worker owns its own SO_REUSEPORT listener and io_uring ring (thread-per-core, shared-nothing, no cross-thread fd handoff); accept, recv, send and close (prep_close) all go through the ring so syscalls are batched. Routes are matched by a comptime router (StaticStringMap for exact paths) with no runtime allocation, connection buffers come from a per-worker demand-paged slab, and pipelined responses are staged and leave as one send. The HttpArena H1 entry also turns off the Date header and caps response headers, so each reply is about 63-66 bytes against about 135 for nginx.
when_to_use: A new Linux service written in Zig that needs plaintext HTTP/1.1 throughput at or above nginx with a custom C module (HttpArena baseline-4096: 4.44M vs 3.28M req/s, 1.35x)
Many keep-alive connections with small responses on a many-core box, where per-core io_uring loops pay off (pipelined-4096: 58.8M req/s, 1.35x libreactorng)
h2c JSON APIs or HTTP/3 baseline traffic where you want one pure-Zig stack with no OpenSSL or C QUIC library to vendor
Projects that want server and matching clients for HTTP, gRPC, WebSocket, SSE, raw TCP/UDP and FIX from one library with one config vocabulary
when_not_to_use: C or C++ codebases: it is a Zig source module consumed through build.zig.zon, with no C ABI library to link
TLS static-file serving: in static-tls-1024 zix came last (339,689 req/s vs nginx 720,869, mongoose 611,058 and agensio 1,191,970)
HTTP/2 over TLS at small payloads, where h2o (16.1M vs 14.1M req/s at baseline-h2-256) and agensio are ahead, and h2c baseline where agensio leads at every connection count
Non-Linux production: .EPOLL and .URING are rejected off Linux and only .ASYNC runs there; Windows, macOS and the BSDs are cross-compile only with no maintainer

Anything needing API stability: pre-1.0 (0.5.0, released 2026-08-17), about 4,950 commits since March 2026, a breaking-changes tracker on Codeberg, one maintainer, and an unaudited from-scratch TLS, QUIC and brotli

integration.dependencies: none (Zig standard library only; build step generates the brotli dictionary)
integration.platforms: x86_64-linux and aarch64-linux maintained; Windows, macOS, FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD cross-compile only with .ASYNC dispatch
integration.thread_safety: Shared-nothing per worker under .EPOLL/.URING (per-worker response cache, slab and ring, no locks); handlers run on worker threads; Logger documented safe from background threads

gotchas: Harness flaw in the static-h2 (and static-h3) rows: the HttpArena zix-http2 and zix-http3 entries scan /data/static with getdents64 at startup (prewarmStatic) and read every file and its .br/.gz twin into process-lifetime buffers that are never revalidated. HttpArena's static-h2 and static-h3 rules for engines say the cache 'must be the framework's own rather than one assembled in the entry, and it must follow the disk'; validate.sh runs its disk-staleness probe only for static-tls, so this is not caught. The static-h2-256 win (1,692,045 req/s vs agensio 1,571,021 and nginx 802,090, which sendfiles per request with no open_file_cache) rests on an entry-built cache the profile forbids.

json-h2c is not like-for-like against nginx: zix-http2's dataset.zig pre-renders each item's JSON fields at startup and only appends total per request, while the nginx module ngx_sprintf-serializes every field per request; engines have no json-h2c rules, and agensio uses the same prefix trick, so the 1.64x over agensio is fair but the 4.0x over nginx compares different work. The H1 json-tls entry, by contrast, serializes every field per request through jzon.

The HttpArena H1 entry sets send_date_header = false and writes a hard-coded 66-byte /pipeline response; nginx sends Date and Server headers. RFC 9110 requires Date from an origin server with a clock, so production zix configs with the header on will write more bytes per response than the benchmarked one.

When io_uring is unavailable (old kernel, low RLIMIT_MEMLOCK, sandbox) .URING silently folds to .EPOLL with only a log notice; the response cache (off in the benchmark) works only under .EPOLL/.URING and keys on method, path and query, so it must not be used for responses that vary by header or cookie.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick zix over libxev (an event loop only, tied at 4.38M req/s baseline-4096) or zeemo (4.42M, a tie) when you need a complete pure-Zig protocol stack with HTTP/2, HTTP/3, gRPC and TLS rather than just an H1 loop; on H1 plaintext it is in the same band as vanilla (V, 4.31M), ioxide (4.11M) and the C# minima-sync entry (4.39M), so the choice there is language, not speed.
verified_claims_summary: In HttpArena on a Threadripper PRO 3995WX (64 cores, kernel 6.17, Docker), zix built with Zig 0.16.0 --release=fast (x86_64_v3+aes+pclmul+adx, musl) served 4.44M req/s at baseline-4096 against nginx 1.31.4 (C module, -O3 -march=native) at 3.28M (1.35x), h2o 3.64M and Drogon 2.02M, but only 1-4% over the io_uring C servers libreactorng and libioma; best-of-3 runs of 5 s, each entry's results file saved at a different time. It loses on baseline-h2 to h2o, on baseline-h2c and static-h3 to agensio, and comes last in static-tls; its static-h2 win uses an entry-built in-memory file cache that the profile rules forbid.
status_note: Very active (last mirror commit 2026-09-05, Codeberg is the main repository) single-maintainer BSD-3-Clause Zig module at 0.5.0, copyable but pre-1.0 with announced breaking changes and the benchmark built from an unpinned branch.
